a regeneration must never touch. _registry.py merges it in; it never writes here.
GHOST VALUES are the standard example values a function is demonstrated with. They cannot be
derived from a contract -- a contract states that a parameter is a `decimal`, not that 1.0 is
a sensible one to show. They exist so that every consumer demonstrates a function the SAME
way, and so a tooltip or a ZBOM can render a real preview before a user has typed anything.
THE SAME SET FEEDS BOTH the execution shape and the INFO preview. That is the point: if the
preview renders a sensible sentence from these values, the wiring resolved -- names, arity,
types and the contract's own reading of the operation. A correct preview is evidence of
correct wiring, which is what makes hovering a button a substitute for testing it.
PLACEHOLDERS IN ANGLE BRACKETS are resolved by the consumer at render time, because they
depend on who is connected: <resident-account>, <wealthiest-patron>, <selected-token>,
<selected-pool>. Anything else is a literal.
SEEDING: harvest from the ZBOM that already wires a function -- those values were chosen
deliberately. Author the rest as each button is wired, so wiring a button and giving it ghost
values are one act rather than two.
partitionNote: HAND-AUTHORED, like `ghost` above, and for the same reason: a contract states that a parameter
THREE KINDS OF SPLIT, and the kind is the first thing to read (owner ruling, 2026-10-27).
kind=list          The list is an ARGUMENT. A client cuts it, the piece count comes from
MEASUREMENT and is unbounded, and the pieces are independent (shape
=partition) or feed back round by round (shape=reduction).
kind=cursor        The work is list-shaped but the list lives in chain STATE -- this
entrypoint takes no list. A pager advances stored progress: unbounded
calls, STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL, repeat until the progress read says done.
kind=architectural The operation decomposes into ORDERED PHASES intrinsic to itself, each
depending on what the last left behind. That is continuation state, so a
defpact is its only expression. DERIVED by inverting the defpact's own
`preferInstead`; never authored here.
WHY A DEFPACT CANNOT CARRY A LIST SPLIT: its step count is fixed by its definition and a list
has no fixed length. A 2-step twin caps the work at two steps forever. That is why the two AQP
defpacts are recorded as SUPERSEDED rather than as architectural routes.
ABSENCE STILL MEANS DO NOT SPLIT. A consumer finding no block sends one transaction or
refuses. 105 entrypoints take a list; only the ones read are classified.
shape=partition  cutting the axis yields pieces whose combined effect equals the one call.
One round, order-independent, fire them all at once.
shape=reduction  each piece yields a NEW intermediate that must be fed back in. Parallel
WITHIN a round, strictly sequential BETWEEN rounds, and the next round's
arguments do not exist until the current one lands on chain.
lockstep         parameters POSITIONAL against the axis, which must be cut WITH it. The
failure here is silent: two arrays that line up by length and are
misaligned move the wrong amount to the wrong place, with no error.
HELD FOR AN OWNER RULING -- the six AQP batch drain/vacate fed slices:
CCp_BatchDrain{TrueFungible,OrtoFungible,Collectable}
CCp_BatchVacate{TrueFungible,OrtoFungible,Collectables}
They look like clean per-leg fan-outs and they are NOT obviously so. BatchDrain's own INFO_
reads "settle-on-last-drain only for beneficiaries fully drained THIS ROUND (live UserUnn)",
which is a CROSS-LEG condition: splitting one beneficiary's legs across two transactions
changes when -- or whether -- the settle fires. The vacate trio carries a "per-beneficiary
score unwind" with the same question, since a beneficiary appearing in two slices has it run
twice and nothing read here says that is idempotent.
It probably converges: UserUnn reaches zero only after the last leg, whichever order they land
atomic operation into a partially-applied one, and these are the ops that move staked assets
out of a pool. Unclassified until read properly -- which costs a client nothing today, because
Cp_WipeSlice (DPOF/DPSF/DPNF) -- the slicer is ON CHAIN (URHC_BuildWipeSlicePlan, named in
fedParams.slicedBy). A client asks for slices; it must not invent them.
CCp_{SweepRecomputeChunk,InjectFixChunk,UnstaleAll} -- cursor pagers, mode
indirect-sequential. They take a chunk SIZE, not a list, and firing two concurrently races
the stored cursor. Correctly described already; a partition block would be a licence to do
the one thing they forbid.
CCp_ReleaseSpecialCustodial -- no list parameter, so there is nothing to cut.

TS01-C1.DPTF|C_BulkTransfer.reason: Each leg of a bulk/multi transfer is an independent debit-credit against a distinct recipient (or a distinct token), so the union of two batches moves exactly what one call would. The sender's total is checked per call, which splitting cannot evade: the sum across batches is the same sum. PARTIAL COMPLETION IS THE ONE REAL DIFFERENCE -- one transaction is atomic, k are not, so a refused batch leaves some recipients paid and some not. That is acceptable for a transfer fan-out and is NOT acceptable for an op whose legs are priced against each other; it is why liquidity ops are absent from this file.

TS01-C2.VST|C_Merge.rounds: Re-read the holder's nonce set after the round settles and merge again until one nonce remains. The round count is NOT known in advance -- it follows from the per-transaction capacity, which is measured -- and the next round's nonce ids do not exist until this one lands, because XIv_MergeNonces mints at (+ 1 nonces-used).
TS01-C2.VST|C_Merge.reason: Every input nonce is WIPED and ONE new nonce is minted carrying the pooled locked amount and the amount-weighted mean unlock time (VST.XIv_MergeNonces -> UC_MergeAll). So a batch does not complete the operation, it reduces it: 860 nonces at 123 per call leaves 7, which are merged again. ROUNDS ARE EXACT, NOT APPROXIMATE -- the weight is sum(balance x stu) / sum(balance), a true weighted mean, and round 1 mints an ABSOLUTE release-date, so wall-clock passing between rounds does not shift it. The only drift is the floor() to whole seconds, once per round, under a second each.

note: Defpacts whose `preferInstead` twin must NOT be given a derived architectural route.
A defpact expresses an ARCHITECTURAL split: ordered phases intrinsic to the operation,
a count fixed by its own definition. These two were written for work that is really
LIST-SHAPED -- unbounded, its length decided by chain state -- and a fixed 2-step
defpact caps that at two steps forever. They are superseded by cursor pagers, which
are unbounded by construction, and the twins carry `kind: cursor` instead.
Owner, 2026-10-27: "we also have the last 2 defpacts which are not architectural but
list based which is why defpacts is not ideal for list based split because the list can
be longer than the number of steps defined in the defpacts" -- and, on why they exist
at all: "i dont even know why we made them in the first place". They are the first
attempt, kept deployed because a deployed module cannot be removed.
